1.explanation: Both group.jsx and sub-menu.jsx walk through this.props.children and call React.cloneElement (or read child.props) on every item, without filtering out text nodes. Any extra whitespace between tag boundaries becomes a string child and causes child.props to be undefined. These two files need to be changed to filter React.Children.toArray(children).filter(React.isValidElement) (or skip non-elements) before mapping/cloning.
1.bug_scenario: When you give a <Menu.Group> (or inline <Menu.SubMenu>) a ‘label’ and then put its <Item> children on the same line separated by a space, that space is parsed as a text node child. In Group.render (and similarly in SubMenu.render), the code blindly does React.Children.map over all children, and for each child it tries to read child.props.className (or cloneElement expecting a React element). Since the first child is actually a plain string (" "), child.props is undefined and you get “Cannot read property 'className' of undefined”.

2.explanation: Both src/nav/group.jsx and src/nav/sub-nav.jsx are responsible for rendering Nav.Group and Nav.SubNav children. In each file the code iterates over this.props.children and expects every child to be a React element with a props.className. Whitespace-only text nodes or other non-element children have no props object, so accessing props.className blows up. These are the files to update (by filtering out text children or guarding child.props) to fix the bug.
2.bug_scenario: In the reproduction code the user is rendering a Nav with a Group wrapper around an Item. Because of the literal newline/space characters between the Group tags and the Item tag, React is inserting text nodes (whitespace) into Group’s children array. Inside src/nav/group.jsx, the Group.render method blindly maps over all children and immediately does child.props.className (and similar) without checking for non-element nodes. When it encounters a text node, child.props is undefined, so accessing className throws “Cannot read property 'className' of undefined.”
